slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Geometric design means choosing shapes and dimensions that meet constraints: a fixed volume, a budget of material, a maximum height.

Example: a box with a square base must hold 1,000 cm3. A 10 by 10 by 10 cube uses 600 cm2 of cardboard; a 20 by 20 by 2.5 box uses 1,000 cm2. Among rectangular boxes with a given volume, the cube uses the least material. A cylinder can do better still. Sketch, compute, compare, and justify every number in the design.
